source.title: PROGRESS IN THE OPEN PROBLEMS IN THEORY OF FUNCTIONS OF BOUNDED INDEX

accepted.question_text: Let L: C^n → R_+ be a positive continuous function, and for a nonzero direction b ∈ C^n define the directional derivatives by ∂F/∂b = Σ_{j=1}^n b_j ∂F/∂z_j and ∂^kF/∂b^k by iterating this operator. An entire function F on C^n is said to have bounded L-index in the direction b if there exists m_0 such that for every m and every z, the normalized derivative (1/(m! L(z)^m))|∂^mF(z)/∂b^m| is bounded above by the maximum of the same normalized quantities for orders 0 through m_0. Suppose P_1(z_1,z_2) and P_2(z_1,z_2) are entire functions of bounded L-index in the coordinate directions e_1=(1,0) and e_2=(0,1), respectively. For which directions b, and under what additional assumptions, must every entire solution F of the first-order partial differential equation P_1(z_1,z_2) ∂F/∂z_1 + P_2(z_1,z_2) ∂F/∂z_2 = h(z_1,z_2) also have bounded L-index in the direction b?
accepted.context_brief: Bounded directional index for PDE solutions

Let us consider the following partial differential equation P1(z1, z2) ∂F/∂z1 + P2(z1, z2) ∂F/∂z2 = h(z1, z2). (1)

Problem 1 ([10, Problem 3]). Let P1(z1, z2), P2(z1, z2) be entire functions of bounded L-index in directions e1 = (1, 0) and e2 = (0, 1) respectively. What are a direction b and additional assumptions such that every entire solution F(z) of equation (1) has a bounded L-index in the direction b?

accepted.question_text: Let b_1,b_2 ∈ C^2 be directions, let g(z_1,z_2) be an entire function of bounded L-index in the directions b_1 and b_2, and interpret bounded L^*-index in a direction b^* by the same directional-derivative criterion as above, with L replaced by L^* and b replaced by b^*. Determine a positive continuous function L^* and a direction b^* such that every entire solution F of the mixed-derivative equation ∂^2F/(∂b_1 ∂b_2) = g(z_1,z_2) has bounded L^*-index in the direction b^*.

Problem 2 ([10, Problem 2]). Let g(z1, z2) be an entire function of bounded L-index in the directions b1 and b2. What are a function L* and a direction b* that an entire solution of equation ∂^2F/∂b1∂b2 = g(z1, z2) has a bounded L*-index in the direction b*?
This means that the problem also requires initial conditions to certainly describe behavior of entire solutions.

accepted.question_text: Let L belong to the class Q_b^n of positive continuous functions for which the regularity quantity λ_b(η) is finite for every η > 0. Is the following criterion equivalent to bounded L-index in the direction b for an entire function F on C^n: there exist constants R > 0, P_2(R) ≥ 1, and η(R) ∈ (0,R) such that for every z_0 ∈ C^n one can choose r = r(z_0) in [η(R), R] with max{|F(z_0 + tb)| : |t| = r/L(z_0)} ≤ P_2(R) min{|F(z_0 + tb)| : |t| = r/L(z_0)}?
accepted.context_brief: Max-min criterion for bounded directional index

evidence.quote: By Q^n_b we denote the class of functions L such that λ(η) is finite for any η > 0.
Problem 4 ([10, Problem 6]). Is Conjecture 1 true?

Conjecture 1. Let L ∈ Q^n_b. An entire function F(z) is of bounded L-index in direction b ∈ C^n if and only if there exist R > 0, P2(R) ≥ 1 and η(R) ∈ (0, R) such that for all z0 ∈ C^n and some r = r(z0) ∈ [η(R), R] inequality max{|F(z0 + tb)|: |t| = r/L(z0)} ≤ P2 min{|F(z0 + tb)|: |t| = r/L(z0)} holds.
Conjecture 1 is completely proved in [7, 11].

accepted.question_text: Let L ∈ Q_b^n, let F be an entire function on C^n, and for r > 0 define G_r^b(F) as the union over zeros z of F of the discs {z + tb : |t| < r/L(z)} along the direction b. For z_0 ∈ C^n, let n_b(r/L(z_0), z_0, 1/F) count the zeros of the slice t ↦ F(z_0 + tb) in the disc |t| ≤ r/L(z_0), and let F(z_0 + tb) ≡ 0 force this quantity to be -1. Is F of bounded L-index in the direction b exactly when both of the following hold: (1) there exist r > 0 and P(r) > 0 such that for every z outside G_r^b(F), the logarithmic directional derivative satisfies |(1/F(z)) ∂F(z)/∂b| ≤ P(r)L(z); and (2) there exist r > 0 and n_e(r) ∈ Z_+ such that for every z_0 with F(z_0 + tb) not identically zero, and every t_0 ∈ C, one has n_b(r/L(z_0), z_0, 1/F) ≤ n_e(r)?

evidence.quote: We denote Gr(F) := G^b_r(F) = ∪_{z : F(z)=0} {z + tb: |t| < r/L(z)}, ... By n_{z0}(r, F) = n^b(r, z0, 1/F) := Σ_{|a^0_k|≤r} 1 we denote the counting function of the zeros ... If for a given z0 ∈ C^n and for all t ∈ C F(z0 + tb) ≡ 0, then we put n_{z0}(r) = −1. Denote n(r) = sup_{z∈C^n} n_z(r/L(z)).
Problem 5 ([10, Problem 7]). Is Conjecture 2 true?

Conjecture 2. Let F(z) be an entire in C^n function, L ∈ Q^n_b and C^n \ G^b_r(F) ≠ ∅. F(z) is a function of bounded L-index in the direction b ∈ C^n if and only if: 1) there exist r > 0, P = P(r) > 0 such that for each z ∈ C^n\G^b_r(F) inequality |(1/F(z)) ∂F(z)/∂b| ≤ P L(z) holds; 2) there exist r > 0, n_e(r) ∈ Z+ such that for every z0 ∈ C^n, for which F(z0 + tb) ≠ 0, and for all t0 ∈ C inequality n_b(r/L(z0), z0, 1/F) ≤ n_e(r) holds.
Note that Conjecture 2 from [10] is proved under the additional restriction 2n(r2)r1 < r2/λ_b(r2). It is currently unknown whether the condition is essential.

accepted.question_text: Let n(r) = sup_{z∈C^n} n_z(r/L(z)), where n_z counts zeros of the slice t ↦ F(z + tb) as above, let λ(r) denote the directional regularity quantity λ_b(r), and set r_0 = sup_{r>0} r/(2 n(r) λ(r)). Do there exist an entire function F on C^n and a continuous function L: C^n → R_+ such that (1) for some r_1 > r_0 and some P > 0, every z outside G_{r_1}^b(F) satisfies (1/|F(z)|)|∂F(z)/∂b| ≤ P L(z), while (2) for every r_2 < r_0 one has sup_{z∈C^n \ G_{r_2}^b(F)} |∂F(z)/∂b|/(|F(z)|L(z)) = +∞ and n(r_2) ∈ (0,+∞)?
accepted.context_brief: Sharp threshold for logarithmic derivative control

Problem 6 ([11, Problem 3]). Denote r0 = sup_{r>0} r/(2n(r)λ(r)). Are there an entire function F in C^n and a continuous function L: C^n → R+ with properties: 1) there exist r1 > r0 and P > 0 such that for each z ∈ C^n\G^b_{r1}(F) 1/|F(z)| |∂F(z)/∂b| ≤ P L(z); 2) for any r2 < r0 sup_{z∈C^n\G^b_{r2}(F)} 1/(|F(z)|L(z)) |∂F(z)/∂b| = +∞ and n(r2) ∈ (0; +∞)?

trace.notes: Mapped the 4-page PDF and identified Problems 1-8 plus Conjectures 1-3 as the likely open-problem regions.
Extracted the first PDE problem and linked it to the bounded directional L-index definition on page 1.
Extracted the mixed-derivative problem and preserved the author's remark that additional initial conditions seem necessary.
Expanded 'Is Conjecture 1 true?' into the full max-min criterion and marked it solved because the paper states it is completely proved.
Expanded the conjecture into a self-contained equivalence using the definitions of G_r^b(F) and the slice zero-counting function from page 2.
Retained the threshold quantity r0 and the two-sided growth conditions from Problem 6.
Moved Problem 3 to needs_review because the source does not define the one-variable notion of bounded l-index explicitly enough to support a fully self-contained rewrite using only this artifact.
Moved Problem 7 to needs_review because the paper states the question briefly but does not unpack the needed one-variable index notions inside this artifact.
Moved Problem 8 to needs_review because 'index boundedness' for analytic functions is not defined inside the four-page source.
